sections.description: The most important words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 5.

sections.title: Grade 4 skills
sections.description: Key words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 4.

questions.question: Which word means 'the ability to take care of yourself and make your own choices'?
questions.options: independence | citizenship | ownership | approval
questions.explanation: Independence is being able to look after yourself and decide things on your own, like planning your own science project.

questions.question: The two groups needed to ___ if they wanted to finish the mural before Friday. Which word fits best?
questions.options: boycott | cooperate | expose | consume
questions.explanation: To cooperate means to work together with others towards the same goal.

questions.question: Nora wrote a letter to ___ the head teacher to open a reading club. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.options: persuade | assume | enquire | navigate
questions.explanation: To persuade someone means to convince them to do or believe something, often by giving good reasons.

questions.question: Which word describes making something sound bigger or more dramatic than it really is?
questions.options: emphasise | exaggerate | encourage | communicate
questions.explanation: To exaggerate means to stretch the truth so something seems more impressive than it actually is.

questions.question: From the top of the hill, the view was ___ — everyone stopped to admire it. Which word fits best?
questions.options: magnificent | innocent | precise | scarce
questions.explanation: Magnificent describes something so beautiful or grand that it impresses everyone who sees it.

questions.question: Which of these sentences states an OPINION rather than a fact?
questions.options: The ancient hall has stood on the hill for centuries. | Some visitors climb the hill every single day. | The hall is the most beautiful building in the whole country. | The hall has no steps leading up to its door.
questions.correctAnswer: The hall is the most beautiful building in the whole country.
questions.explanation: 'Most beautiful' is a feeling, not something that can be proved true or false — that makes it an opinion.

questions.question: Read this: 'The crew checked the equipment twice, because in space even a small mistake can grow into a big problem.' Why did the crew check the equipment twice?
questions.options: Because a small mistake in space can become a big problem | Because they had lost some of their tools | Because their commander was watching them | Because they had extra time before launch
questions.correctAnswer: Because a small mistake in space can become a big problem
questions.explanation: The word 'because' points straight at the reason: in space, small mistakes can turn into big problems.

questions.question: A poster asks, 'Have you ever wondered why our playground is the dirtiest in town?' What is this technique called?
questions.options: A rhetorical question | A call to action | A quote from an expert | A time connective
questions.explanation: A rhetorical question is asked to make the reader think or feel something — it does not expect a spoken answer.

questions.question: A text says: 'She became the first woman to command the space station, and her calm decisions impressed the whole crew.' Is this biography or autobiography?
questions.options: Biography, because it is written about her in the third person | Autobiography, because it is written about her in the third person | Biography, because it uses the word I | Autobiography, because it uses the word I
questions.correctAnswer: Biography, because it is written about her in the third person
questions.explanation: A biography is the story of someone's life written by somebody else, using words like she and her rather than I.

questions.question: Which sentence is a FACT that could be checked and proved?
questions.options: The ancient hall is the most wonderful place in the world. | The ancient hall has stood on the hilltop for centuries. | Everybody should visit the ancient hall at least once. | The ancient hall is far more interesting than any museum.
questions.correctAnswer: The ancient hall has stood on the hilltop for centuries.
questions.explanation: A fact can be checked and proved true — how long a building has stood is something historians can confirm.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: Everyone are ready for the presentation. | Everyone is ready for the presentation. | Everyone were ready for the presentation. | Everyone been ready for the presentation.
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone is ready for the presentation.
questions.explanation: Everyone looks like it means many people, but it is singular, so it takes the singular verb is.

questions.question: If you heat ice, it ___. Which word completes this zero conditional sentence?
questions.options: melting | melted | melts | melt
questions.explanation: The zero conditional uses the present simple in both halves to describe something that is true every single time.

questions.question: Layla has lived in Hargeisa ___ 2020. Which word completes the sentence?
questions.options: since | for | during | ago
questions.explanation: Since points to when something started; for measures how long something has lasted, such as 'for four years'.

questions.question: Which phrase puts the adjectives in the correct order?
questions.options: a beautiful old wooden box | an old wooden beautiful box | a wooden beautiful old box | a beautiful wooden old box
questions.explanation: Adjectives usually line up as opinion, then age, then material: beautiful (opinion), old (age), wooden (material).

questions.question: Which word best signals the FINAL step in a set of instructions?
questions.options: Next | Meanwhile | Finally | While
questions.explanation: Finally is a closing time connective that tells the reader they have reached the last step.

questions.question: Which sentence gives an instruction, the way a recipe step does?
questions.options: She stirs the rice for two minutes. | I stirred the rice for two minutes. | Stir the rice for two minutes. | We might stir the rice for two minutes.
questions.correctAnswer: Stir the rice for two minutes.
questions.explanation: Instructions use imperative verbs — command words like stir, pour or mix — with no subject in front of them.

questions.question: Which sentence is the best CALL TO ACTION to end a persuasive poster?
questions.options: Litter is a problem in many schools around the world. | Some people think tidy playgrounds look nicer. | Bring one bin bag to the main gate at 8 o'clock on Saturday. | Our playground has looked the same for many years.
questions.correctAnswer: Bring one bin bag to the main gate at 8 o'clock on Saturday.
questions.explanation: A call to action tells the reader exactly what to do, when and where — it turns their agreement into action.

questions.question: In a set of written instructions, which part lists everything the reader needs BEFORE the steps begin?
questions.options: The title | The materials list | The numbered steps | The tips
questions.explanation: The materials list gathers everything a reader must collect before starting, so the steps themselves can flow without interruption.

questions.question: Which linking word best ADDS WEIGHT to a persuasive point that comes before it?
questions.options: Furthermore | Meanwhile | However | Yesterday
questions.explanation: Furthermore signals that another strong point is being added to support the argument already made.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the informal, friendly tone and contractions of a blog post?
questions.options: It is important to note that the crew has completed the mission. | You won't believe what happened on my third day! | It is hereby confirmed that the mission was a success. | The mission's completion has been noted by all crew members.
questions.correctAnswer: You won't believe what happened on my third day!
questions.explanation: Blog writing uses a friendly, spoken voice with contractions like won't, so it feels like chatting rather than a report.

questions.question: Which word names a chemical that farmers spray on crops to kill harmful insects?
questions.options: pesticide | debt | famine | labour
questions.explanation: Pesticide is a chemical used to protect crops from insects and weeds, though too much of it can be harmful.

questions.question: Which word names the person who cleans and looks after a school building?
questions.options: merchant | caretaker | senator | messenger
questions.explanation: A caretaker is a person who cleans and takes care of a building, such as a school.

questions.question: Which word describes people travelling to new places for fun or to learn about them?
questions.options: tourism | equator | rental | horizon
questions.explanation: Tourism means travelling to new places, often for fun or to see and learn about them.

questions.question: Which word describes someone who has been forced to leave their country, often because of war or danger?
questions.options: refugee | tenant | consumer | bachelor
questions.explanation: A refugee is someone who has had to leave their home country, often to escape war or danger.

questions.question: Read this: 'Farmers use pesticide because it protects their crops from insects and weeds. However, too much of it can be dangerous, so everyone must wash fruit and vegetables before eating them.' What is ONE danger of pesticide mentioned here?
questions.options: It stops crops from growing at all | It can be dangerous if fruit and vegetables are not washed | It costs farmers too much money | It attracts more insects to the crops
questions.correctAnswer: It can be dangerous if fruit and vegetables are not washed
questions.explanation: The passage says pesticide can be dangerous, which is exactly why fruit and vegetables must be washed before eating.

questions.question: A text titled 'A Trip to the Capital' describes a family's day of sightseeing at museums, a busy railway station and a tall office building. What is the text mainly ABOUT?
questions.options: A family visiting interesting places in a capital city | A family moving house to a new country | Farmers protecting their crops from pests | A family building a new railway station
questions.correctAnswer: A family visiting interesting places in a capital city
questions.explanation: Museums, a railway station and an office building are all places the family visits, so the text is about a day of sightseeing in a capital city.

questions.question: A text compares two neighbours: one is a refugee who fled danger in her home country, and the other is an immigrant who chose to move for a new job. What is the main DIFFERENCE between them, according to the text?
questions.options: One neighbour is much older than the other | One neighbour had to leave, while the other chose to move | One neighbour speaks a different language | One neighbour lives in a bigger house
questions.correctAnswer: One neighbour had to leave, while the other chose to move
questions.explanation: A refugee is forced to leave their country because of danger, while an immigrant chooses to move, often for reasons like work.

questions.question: It ___ rain tomorrow, so take a jacket just in case. Which word shows this is only a POSSIBILITY?
questions.options: must | might | mustn't | is
questions.explanation: Might shows that something is possible but not certain, unlike must, which shows a strong rule.

questions.question: Nora saves her money ___ fresh fruit every week. Which words complete the sentence?
questions.options: to buy | buying | for buy | buy
questions.explanation: The infinitive of purpose uses to plus the base verb to explain why someone does something.

questions.question: This mango is ___ than that one. Which word completes the sentence correctly?
questions.options: sweet | sweeter | more sweet | sweetest
questions.explanation: Short adjectives like sweet add -er to compare two things: sweet becomes sweeter.

questions.question: ___ does rice grow best? Which word completes this question about a place?
questions.options: What | Who | Where | Why
questions.explanation: Where asks about a place, and rice growing well is a question about location.

questions.question: Which sentence could open a set of written instructions for making a snack?
questions.options: Yesterday, I made a snack for my family. | First, wash your hands before you start. | Making snacks is something I enjoy doing. | My favourite snack is a sandwich with cheese.
questions.correctAnswer: First, wash your hands before you start.
questions.explanation: Instructions open with a command word and a time connective like first, telling the reader exactly what to do.

questions.question: Which line would fit best on a health poster encouraging pupils to eat well?
questions.options: Fresh food is better than old food, so choose it every day. | Some pupils eat fresh food sometimes. | Food can be fresh or old, depending on the day. | Fresh food was eaten by pupils yesterday.
questions.correctAnswer: Fresh food is better than old food, so choose it every day.
questions.explanation: A good poster line uses a clear comparison and encourages the reader to act, which is what a persuasive poster needs.

questions.question: A short report explains one benefit of pesticide, one danger of it, and then gives advice. Which sentence is the ADVICE, not a benefit or a danger?
questions.options: Pesticide protects crops from insects and weeds. | Pesticide can be dangerous if it is not washed off. | Everyone must wash fruit and vegetables before eating them. | Pesticide is sprayed onto crops by farmers.
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone must wash fruit and vegetables before eating them.
questions.explanation: Advice tells the reader what they should do, and this sentence uses must to give a clear instruction based on the danger explained earlier.
